scientific_hypothesis: Imposing bilateral symmetry constraints on mirror layer pairs and restricting thickness search to ±5 nm around round-2 medians will reduce the optimization degrees of freedom sufficiently for L-BFGS-B to converge to a locally optimal phase-matched configuration, improving target score without increasing layer count.
expected_advantages: symmetry ensures phase matching between mirrors
bounded search prevents unphysical thickness excursions
known_risks: symmetry constraint may prevent discovery of superior asymmetric solutions
±5 nm bounds may be too restrictive if round-2 medians are suboptimal
expected_observations: If the hypothesis holds, best_target_score should rise as mirror pair thicknesses converge to quarter-wave values at the center passband wavelength, and tightest_margin should remain stable across optimization rounds.
If the hypothesis fails, best_target_score will plateau below 0.5 and valid_candidates will decrease as thickness variations push the cavity resonance outside the 255-280 nm band.
thicknesses_nm should show quarter-wave scaling for mirror layers and approximately half-wave scaling for the defect cavity if the resonance condition is satisfied.
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best.
If valid_candidates falls below 5 for two consecutive rounds, relax the layer thickness bounds by 20% and continue for one more round before stopping.
